question: Does direct East-Asian Cirsium evidence support transporting the existence and context dependence of a flower-head antagonist pathway, while keeping the North-American experimental seed-loss magnitude separate?

focal_taxon_antagonist_channel.attack_rate_definition: emerged insects / collected flower heads x 100

japan_regime_structure.phenology_partition: Larinus latissimus associated with the two spring-blooming Cirsium (C. japonicum and C. brevicaule), whereas L. meleagris primarily used autumn-blooming hosts in central Honshu.
japan_regime_structure.geographic_partition: Urophora sachalinensis occurred mainly on the Pacific side and Xyphosia punctigera mainly on the Japan Sea side of central Honshu; simultaneous occurrence was rare.

japan_display_cost.pattern: predispersal seed predation increased with flower/head production at both populations

existing_experimental_magnitude_anchor.allowed_use: pathway-level fitness magnitude anchor showing that Cirsium reproductive herbivory can be large in experimentally studied systems

allowed: Flower-head antagonist exposure is directly documented in Japanese Cirsium and in the focal Ryukyu taxon C. brevicaule.
Japanese antagonist assemblages are structured by host flowering season and geography rather than behaving as one spatially uniform pressure.
In Japanese C. purpuratum, greater flower production can increase predispersal seed-predator exposure and offset reproductive gains.
These findings strengthen ecological-gate and selection-mosaic hypotheses relative to a single monotonic abiotic-scaling model.
not_allowed: RR=2.674 is the effect size in East Asian Cirsium.
The C. brevicaule attack rate of 26.1 is a 26.1% seed-fitness loss.
Antagonists caused the evolution of white colour, orientation, phyllary posture or stickiness.
Phenology/geography structure identifies disturbance as the causal driver.

decisive_remaining_gap: A focal East-Asian manipulation that reduces flower-head antagonists and measures viable seed/recruitment on ancestry-matched populations; for colour/display questions, the same populations must also quantify pollination assurance and phenotype-specific antagonist exposure.
